newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLO market in battle over 5-yr benchmark.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLO market in battle over 5-yr benchmark.

text.p: A battle in Belgium's linear bond market over which is the current five year benchmark will be fuelled on Monday when the Treasury offers OLO 10 (June 25, 2002) at a regular auction for the first time in four years.
OLO 10, which was last month offered in an exchange auction, is already a highly liquid issue, with more than 330 billion francs outstanding, a Treasury official said.

But the bond was recently skirted by J.P. Morgan, which in January chose OLO 7 (9.00 pct, June 2001) for its MEUS five-year benchmark page. OLO 7 is also liquid, with around 308 billion francs outstanding.

A Treasury official said the market had indicated it wanted OLO 10 to be the new benchmark. But traders at two primary dealers said many players are waiting for the Treasury to start a new five-year benchmark line later this year.
The five year area of the curve remains the most popular among OLO investors.

"We are a bit in between (OLO 7 and 10) at the moment," one trader said. "It's a bit strange (the Treasury) does not want to issue a new five year, December 2001. They will probably issue a new December 2002 at the end of the year so we are not in the same situation next year," one trader said.
